div.head: Leis Wl 45.2
div.ab: E si testimonie ad, si cum nous einz desimes, voest les treis f[e]iz; e a la quart[e] feiz le dereinet u il le rende.
Si uero testes habet, uideant rem tercio; et quarta uice aut rem diracionet aut amittet.
E si testimonie ad, si cum nous einz desimes, voest les treis f[e]iz e a la quart[e] feiz le dereinet u il le rende.

45, 2. Wenn [Besitz]er jedoch [Kauf-]zeugenschaft hat, so wie wir zuvor gesagt haben, ziehe [man] drei Male zur Gewähr; aber beim vierten Male erweise [der Bezogene] es als sein eigen oder derselbe liefere es [dem Anefänger] aus.

45, 2. If, however, the [possess]or has [purchase-]witnesses, as we have said before, [one] shall vouch to warranty three times; but at the fourth time [the man vouched] shall prove it as his own or the same shall deliver it up [to the attacher].

And if he has witnesses in accordance with what we have declared above, vouching to warranty shall take place three times; and on the fourth occasion he shall prove his ownership of it or deliver it up.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 272–273 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text and German translation added from Gesetze I p. 518, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: L und danach Neuere missverstehen ueeir; voist ändert MAT.; allein Cnut’s tyme übersetzt der Lateiner 12. Jhs. (ad)vocet, afz. vocher: (zur Gewähr) rufen; vgl. 21, 3
L, and modern editors after him, misunderstand ueeir; MAT. alters to voist; but the 12th-cent. Latin translator renders Cnut’s tyme by (ad)vocet, OFr. vocher: call (to warranty); cf. 21, 3
